snapshot.title: This month's snapshot
snapshot.noSnapshot: Your snapshot appears once you have added income or expenses.
snapshot.noPrevious: Your first month. From next month this card shows what changed.

indicators.title: Six things to watch
indicators.intro: Each one has a plain definition. Open it to see how the number is made and where to change the data behind it.

emergency.title: Emergency fund
emergency.value: {count, plural, =1 {# month} other {# months}} of essentials
emergency.definition: Liquid savings (cash, bank balances, deposits and liquid funds with no lock-in) divided by one month of essential spending including loan instalments. Six months is the usual target; three for a dual-income household with stable jobs.

cashflow.title: Cash flow
cashflow.definition: Take-home income minus all spending and instalments, as a share of take-home. Twenty percent is a healthy floor; what is left is what can go to goals.

debt.title: Debt burden
debt.definition: All loan instalments divided by take-home income. Lenders stop at about 40%; under 30% leaves room for everything else. High-cost debt (over 15% or a revolving card balance) is flagged separately in the net worth view.

goals.title: Goals
goals.definition: A goal is on track when what is assigned to it plus its monthly investment, grown at the expected return of its mix, reaches the inflated target by the date. The share here counts goals, not rupees.

retirement.title: Retirement
retirement.definition: A projection: retirement savings and long-term investments grown to retirement age, plus the retirement SIP, against the corpus that would fund today's spending (inflated) from retirement to age 85. Over 100% means on course; it moves with every assumption in the rule pack.

data.title: Data completeness
data.definition: How much of the profile and the six data families is filled in, weighted by what the check-up needs most. Every other indicator is only as good as this one.

actions.title: Top three actions
actions.empty: Run a check-up to get your actions.
actions.allDone: Every plan item is done or parked. Re-run the check-up to refresh it.

goalsTable.title: Goals
goalsTable.projectedNote: Target and progress are projections at the expected return of each goal's mix.
goalsTable.empty: No goals yet. A goal is an amount on a date; the planner does the rest.

trends.title: Trends
trends.intro: One point per month, from your monthly snapshots.
trends.waiting: Trend lines appear once you have two months of snapshots. Your first one is saved; the next is taken automatically at the start of next month.

netWorth.title: Net worth
netWorth.intro: What you own, what you owe, and how much of it you could reach in a week.
netWorth.empty: Add assets, investments or loans to see your net worth.
netWorth.liquidShare: {pct}% of assets can be sold within a week
netWorth.concentrationCategory: {category} is {pct}% of your assets. Above 60% in one category, a bad year for that category is a bad year for you.
netWorth.concentrationItem: "{label}" alone is {pct}% of your assets. One holding above 40% is a concentration risk.
netWorth.noConcentration: No single category or holding dominates your assets.
netWorth.liquidRule: How liquid net worth is counted
netWorth.liquidRuleBody: Liquid net worth = assets you could turn into cash within about a week, minus what you must pay within a year. Counted in: cash, bank balances, fixed deposits, receivables, mutual funds, stocks, ETFs, bonds and gold that are not marked illiquid or locked in. Never counted, whatever was entered: your home and other property, land, vehicles, business equity, EPF, PPF, NPS, ULIPs, savings-type insurance and alternatives. Subtracted: credit-card and buy-now-pay-later balances, and any loan with twelve or fewer months left.
netWorth.realEstateNote: Real estate never counts as cash. It is in your net worth, not in your liquid net worth.
